s.en: The day until the appointed hour was terribly long.
Not a word of her lessons went in, and in workshop she dropped screws on the floor three times.
Instructor Regen said nothing, though she had a feeling those sleepy eyes had rested on her, just once, for a long moment.
At lunch the three of them held a quick council behind the library building.
"I shall be coming too."
"But it's the lower ring, in the middle of the night. Someone like you walking around would stick out a mile."
"Fear not. I possess at least some knowledge of disguise."
"...I've got nothing but worries."
Niko's job was the route and the gear.
An old map of the service tunnels, a steam lantern, rope, and a strange cylindrical device he called his "secret weapon."
"What's that?"
"Flash tube. Pull the cord and it lights up like midday. ...Probably."
"Probably?"
"Never tested it. So the best outcome is we don't need it."
That night Sera lay on her bed fully dressed, counting the stains on the ceiling and waiting for the time to pass.
Half past two.
She crept down the stairs, and as she put her hand to the shop door, a floorboard creaked behind her.
She turned; Oz stood in the doorway of the back room, a lamp in his hand.
He'd thrown an old work coat over his nightclothes, and wore his usual sour expression.
Caught, Sera thought, bracing herself.
But her grandfather neither scolded her nor demanded to know where she was going.
"Got the key?"
"...Yeah."
"The watch?"
"I've got it."
Oz studied her face for a while, then gave a small nod and held out what he had in his hand.
A pair of worn leather gloves. Only the fingertips had been re-patched with brand-new leather.
"Elise's. She wore these too, whenever she went out at night."
"You come back. Understand?"
Sera gripped the gloves tight and nodded without a word.
Never once, since her mother had gone, had Sera heard her grandfather speak that name like this.
At night, the lower ring wears a completely different face.
The factory chimneys slept; in their place, mist rising off the canals blurred the light of the gas lamps.
Laughter leaking from a tavern's back door, a stray cat yowling somewhere, her own footsteps striking the cobbles.
Niko was already waiting at the foot of the bridge where they'd agreed to meet.
On his back he carried a bag stuffed to bursting with tools.
"You made it. No sign of Her Ladyship yet."
Before he'd finished speaking, a figure came towards them out of the mist.
A plain mouse-grey coat and a hat pulled low over the eyes.
At a glance, any ordinary girl of the town.
— so long as you didn't watch her walk.
Spine ramrod straight, gliding over the cobbles, she was, however you looked at it, a noblewoman crossing a ballroom.

t: お待たせいたしました
s.en: "I do apologise for keeping you waiting."
"...Where'd the 'knowledge of disguise' go?"
"Did you say something?"
"Nope. Nothing."
Following Niko, the three of them made their way down narrow canal-side alleys.
The way grew gradually narrower and darker, until every trace of other people was gone.
Over a rusted iron fence, down a crumbling flight of stone steps — and there it was.
Half-buried in the canal wall, an old iron door kept its mouth quietly shut.
On the plate nailed above the door, all that could be read in faded letters was "No. 7."
"This is it. Old Maintenance Gate No. 7."
When Sera saw the keyhole, her breath caught.
It was no ordinary keyhole. The same crest as on the watch lid was cut shallowly into the iron plate, and a small hole was bored through its centre.
Sera took out the pocket watch.
Though the hands were still running backwards, the time they showed was, for some reason, exactly right. 3:16.
The thin second hand crept towards seventeen past, one mark at a time.
"...3:17. The hour in the letter."
The three of them waited, holding their breath.
Click.
The instant the minute hand touched seventeen, the crest on the door took on the same blue glow as the markings on the watch.
With shaking hands, Sera slid the brass key in.
Before she could turn it, the key turned by itself.
With a heavy groan, the door swung slowly inward.
Inside, it was far roomier than she'd expected.
The brick ceiling was high, and thick pipes ran in rows along the walls.
And twining around those pipes, strand upon strand of blue light stretched away into the depths of the tunnel.
"...The roots of the time crystal."
Viola's voice was barely a whisper.
"The tower's crystal is rooted deep underground. All the time in Vern flows out to the city through these roots."
"So if we follow these..."
"...we end up right under the tower."
Niko raised the steam lantern, and with the glowing roots as their guide, the three of them went deeper into the tunnel.
Their footsteps echoed back off the damp walls, over and over.
The further they went, the thicker and brighter the roots grew.
But Sera had noticed: every so often the light flickered irregularly, nearly went out, then rallied again.
Like the failing pulse of someone very ill.
How long had they been walking?
Suddenly the tunnel opened out.
Into a large round chamber.
From ceiling to floor, countless glowing roots poured down like a waterfall, all flowing into something set at the chamber's centre.
It looked like a tall, old pendulum clock.
Except that its face had no numerals; in their place were the same twelve fine marks as on Sera's watch.
And the pendulum didn't swing side to side: it turned, slowly, in a circle.
"What is this... who'd put something here?"
That was when Sera took a step closer.
The watch in her breast pocket gave a hard, heavy throb.
As if in answer, the face of the pendulum clock blazed blue.
Light filled the chamber, and within it, the figure of a woman took shape.
She wore work clothes, her hair tied back in one.
Her translucent outline wavered uncertainly, and yet her features were startlingly like the ones Sera saw in the mirror every morning.
The woman didn't answer.
She wasn't looking at Sera. Her eyes were fixed on somewhere far away, somewhere that wasn't here.
"It's an echo..."
Viola whispered.
"A time-echo. An old art that burns a moment of the past into a place. I had only ever read of it in books."
The woman in the light — Elise — began to speak.
"Sera. If you're hearing this, then that watch has started moving."
"I'm sorry. For leaving without telling you anything."

t: 行かなければならなかった
s.en: "But I had to go, no matter what. To stop the thing that's eating away at the time crystal."
Like an old gramophone, the voice crackled and broke off here and there.
"The crystal isn't weakening on its own. Someone is stealing the city's time, little by little."
"I'm following it to its source... I've decided to go a long way back."
"A long way... back?"
"The watch will protect you. But don't overuse it. For every bit of time you turn back, your own time gets whittled away."
"And, Sera — the man in the grey mask, you must—"
There the voice cut off.
The echo's outline began to come apart like sand.
"Wait! Mom, I still—"
Her outstretched fingertips passed straight through the motes of light.
As she faded, Elise seemed to turn, just once at the end, and look back.
Whether she was smiling or crying, Sera couldn't tell.
The light went out, and all that remained in the chamber was the pulse of the roots.
"—Too late, then."
At the voice behind them, the three spun round as if struck.
A grey shadow stood at the mouth of the tunnel.
Grey greatcoat. Grey mask.
In his hand, a silver pocket watch was ticking the right way round.
"Who the hell are you!"
Niko levelled his flash tube; Viola opened her fan.
The sigil carved into the ribs of the fan glowed a pale violet.
"It was I who sent the letter. An echo will open only for one of Rewinder blood, you see."
"So the 'E'..."
"I apologise for borrowing the name. But had I not, you would never have come."
The man stepped slowly into the chamber.
"Halt!"
Viola swept her fan.
Violet light flashed out, and the time around the man grew heavy and slow, as if sunk in honey.
It was a brilliant piece of work, worthy of the top of the Chronomancy course.
And yet the man didn't so much as twitch an eyebrow.
He pressed the crown of his silver watch lightly with his thumb.
That was all.
Sound vanished from the world.
The light loosed from Viola's fan hung frozen in the air.
Niko's arm, halfway through pulling the cord of the flash tube, the cascading light of the roots — everything had stopped.
— Just like what happened in the tower.
But one thing was different.
Sera could move.
In her breast pocket the watch had grown hot enough to burn, and it was hammering out its backward beat.
Behind the mask, the man's eyes widened slightly.
"You move within stopped time. Not even Elise could do that."
"Are you the one stealing the crystal's time?"
Sera forced down the tremor in her voice.
"Mom said she went to stop it."
"Half right. Half wrong."
"I am not stealing time. But I know who is. And — very likely — where your mother is now."
"Where?!"
"If you wish to know, come with me."
The man held out a gloved hand.
In the stopped world, only that hand looked strangely real.
If she went, she might see her mother.
The answer to the question she'd dreamt about again and again since her mother vanished might be right there.
But Sera's eyes were on the violet light frozen in the air, and on Niko's hand, still gripping the flash tube.
Two people who had trusted her enough to follow her all the way down here.
"...I'm not going."
"I'm not leaving these two behind to go off with someone I know nothing about."
For a while the man said nothing.
Then a low laugh escaped from behind the mask.
"You are Elise's daughter after all."
"Very well. Tonight I came only to confirm."
The man pressed the crown again.
Sound came back to the world.
The violet light lanced through empty air.
Niko's flash tube let loose a tremendous blaze.
When their seared-white vision finally returned, the grey man was nowhere to be seen.
"...It actually worked."
"Is this the time to be impressed?! Who on earth was that man..."
Sera stopped Viola mid-sentence with a raised hand.
She wasn't hurt, but her legs were shaking badly.
Was it the price of moving inside stopped time, or just plain fear?
Either way, she didn't want to stay here a second longer.
As they turned to go back, Niko stopped short in front of the pendulum clock.
He held up the lantern and ran a finger along the side of the base.
"Hey, Sera. There's something carved here."
When he brushed away the soot, a small nameplate appeared.
A maker's name, and a date.
"Made by Elise Milford. Royal Calendar 302."
"...That's impossible."
Viola's voice came out hoarse.
"This is the year 402. That is a date — from a hundred years ago."
A hundred years ago.
The year the Rewinders vanished from the records, every last one of them.
"I've decided to go a long way back" — her mother's voice from the echo came back to her, deep in her ears.
In her breast pocket, as if nothing had happened, the watch went on ticking backwards.
